No source read gives its fate or the round KPCB China entered, so status unknown and stage undetermined.

KPCB China holding (X1, provisional IN): a Shanghai IPTV platform and broadband content provider, on the firm's 2008-10 China listing (location 'Shanghai, China') and its 2012-14 company pages under Teams China. No source read gives its fate or the round KPCB China entered, so status unknown and stage undetermined.

KPCB China holding (X1, provisional IN): a Beijing provider of wireless data applications for financial institutions, on the firm's 2008-10 China listing (location 'Beijing, China') and its 2012-14 company pages under Teams China. No source read gives its fate or the round KPCB China entered, so status unknown and stage undetermined.

KPCB China holding (X1, provisional IN): the 2013-14 company page lists it under Teams China with partner James Huang. Its own site (Omni Pharma, inhalation drug delivery) carries a Shanghai ICP filing and 2024 regulatory news, so it operates; a 2024 'potential unicorn' award is not a mark. The round is not on record.

OriGene (cDNA clones and research reagents, Rockville MD, founded 1996; its site still operates). The firm's 2013-14 page names James Huang, KPCB China's life-sciences partner, so the position is read as a KPCB China one and flagged for the X1 count; the round is not on record.

NovaDigm Therapeutics (fungal and bacterial vaccines, the NDV-3 programme), on the firm's 2012 company page under Life Sciences. Its old domain now shows an unrelated telemedicine page (read 2026-09-30); no source read gives its fate, its city or the round the firm entered.

Ogin, formerly FloDesign Wind Turbine (shrouded mixer-ejector wind turbines, Massachusetts), on the firm's 2014-18 pages with Bill Joy, John Doerr and Jan van Dokkum. The company wound down around 2015-16 and its fdwt.com domain is parked for sale (checked 2026-09-30); the round the firm entered is not cited, so undetermined. Confidence on the status is medium.

Omio (GoEuro until 2019), multimodal travel booking, headquartered in Berlin (Wikipedia). KPCB's growth team led GoEuro's 2015 round of about $70M, after the 2013-14 seed and first institutional rounds; Wikipedia names the 2018 $150M round the Series C, so the 2015 entry is a Series B (Growth). A Digital Growth Fund position is IN (D2). No priced mark at or above $1B is cited (2022 Series E of $80M).

Omnifold, AI models trained per customer for supply-chain forecasting, San Francisco. The firm dates its entry 2025 (site since-year); Lightspeed's card says Series A 2025, but no source read names the round Kleiner Perkins entered, so undetermined. Momentum check 2026-09-30: the company's own post (2026-06-26) announces a $30M Series B at a $300M valuation, $60M raised in total, backed by Kleiner Perkins and Lightspeed; no $1B round. A Google News query returned nothing.

ON Technology, founded 1987 by Mitch Kapor (network and desktop systems management software, Massachusetts); public, then acquired by Symantec on 2003-10-27 (Wikipedia). The round the firm entered is not on record.

One True Media, online video and slideshow creation, Redwood City (the firm's 2008-10 listing). Its site no longer answers (2026-09-30) and no source read gives its fate or the round the firm entered.

OneLogin, identity and access management, founded 2009 in San Francisco; acquired by One Identity on 2021-10-04 (Wikipedia; the firm's exit line). The firm dates its entry 2013; TechCrunch's 2019 report of the $100M round does not name Kleiner Perkins and no source read names the 2013 round, so undetermined.
OnFiber Communications, metro fiber-optic access networks, acquired by Qwest in 2006; the firm's 2008-10 listing places it in Denver, Qwest's home. The round the firm entered is not on record.

OnFiber Communications, metro fiber-optic access networks, acquired by Qwest in 2006; the firm's 2008-10 listing places it in Denver, Qwest's home. The round the firm entered is not on record. This row is the same company as onfiber-communications-inc (the 2012 page's name carries stray non-breaking-space codes); the two should merge.

Onyx Pharmaceuticals, South San Francisco; formed in 1992 with money from Chiron and the venture firms Avalon, IVP, J. H. Whitney and Kleiner Perkins (Wikipedia); IPO 1996, acquired by Amgen in 2013. The formation round is not named, so the stage is undetermined; below_1b as an acquired row.
Opcom, voice messaging systems; the firm dates its entry 1982 and records the exit as acquired by Octel. No source read gives the round or the company's city.

Open Raven, cloud data security, Los Angeles. The firm's post of 2020-06-16 says Kleiner Perkins led the Series A; the firm's listings begin in 2021 and no earlier Kleiner Perkins round is known, so the Series A is read as the entry. Its domain no longer resolves (2026-09-30) and no sale or shutdown was found, so status unknown.

Opower, utility customer-engagement software for energy efficiency, Arlington VA. Wikipedia: the $50M third round of November 2010 was led by Accel and KPCB. The 2014 S-1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1412043/000119312514079317/d620747ds1.htm) lists the stake as held by KPCB Green Growth Fund (2,247,192 shares, the same as Accel's, bought in that round) and dates the amended investor rights agreement 2010-11-24. Growth. Acquired by Oracle in 2016.

funding_rounds.lead: Accel Partners; Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers

note: Ophthonix (iZon high-resolution lenses), which the firm's own 2012 page calls 'a San Diego based vision correction company' (partner Joe Lacob, a seat from his Kleiner Perkins years). No source read gives its fate or the round.

Optic, Inc. (Andrey Doronichev), founded 2022 on AI content recognition for NFTs. The Block (2022-07-20): an $11M seed led by Kleiner Perkins and Pantera Capital, with Greylock among the others. optic.xyz now redirects to BIOPTIC, AI research for pharma teams, whose 2026 footer still reads 'Optic, Inc.' (read 2026-09-30): the same company as Greylock's Optic row (San Francisco, Healthcare & Bio, aligned); not the YC Optic (New York, acquired). Graduation left for the graduation pass.
Optilink, fiber-optic loop transmission equipment, Petaluma CA; the firm dates its entry 1987 and records the exit to Digital Switch (DSC Communications). The round is not on record.

Orcan Energy AG, waste-heat-to-power ORC modules; its own site (read 2026-09-30) says headquartered in Munich with production in Kiel, and it operates. On the firm's 2013-18 greentech pages (Brook Porter, Jan van Dokkum); the round is not on record.

OtisMed, patient-specific knee-surgery instrumentation (Alameda CA); the firm's own 2012-14 page calls it a business unit of Stryker Orthopaedics (acquired 2009). Partner Dana Mead. The round is not on record.

OUYA (Boxer8, Santa Monica), the Android game console; its software assets and team were sold to Razer in July 2015 (Wikipedia), an asset sale read as acquired with Razer the successor. Partner Bing Gordon; the Kleiner Perkins round is not cited (the queued Google News check had not returned), so undetermined.

Oven, the company behind the Bun JavaScript runtime (Jarred Sumner). The firm's post of 2025-12-02 says 'we proudly led Bun (then called Oven's) Seed'; Wikipedia dates the $7M seed led by Kleiner Perkins to 2022-08-24. Anthropic acquired Bun on 2025-12-02 (Wikipedia). Graduation left for the graduation pass.

Packagd (shoppable unboxing video), incubated at Kleiner Perkins by partner Eric Feng. TechCrunch (2017-06-08): Kleiner Perkins put up the initial $1.5M, then Forerunner and GV led a $6M Series A, which graduates the row. The seed is dated only as before that article, so the entry year is 2017 at the latest. Facebook bought it in 2019 (GV's row, aligned). No source read gives the city.

Pair Team, primary care for Medicaid patients, San Francisco. HIT Consultant (2020-12-09): out of stealth with a $2.7M seed from Kleiner Perkins, Craft Ventures and Y Combinator. The company's release of 2023-10-19 names a $9M Series A led by NEXT Ventures with Kleiner Perkins participating: graduated.

Parallel Web Systems (Parag Agrawal), web infrastructure for AI agents; the AU claim is a Wikidata homonym, disputed: a US company. TechCrunch (2026-04-29): $100M Series B at $2B led by Sequoia, after a $100M Series A at $740M led by Kleiner and Index (the firm's own post of 2025-11-12 says it co-led the Series A; its since-year is 2025, and the January 2024 seed was Khosla, Index and First Round). Mark aligned with Spark and First Round. The careers page lists Palo Alto first among its offices (Spark's city; First Round reads San Francisco). Momentum slice: the mark itself is the check.

Pathlight (Alex Kvamme, Trey Doig), team performance management for customer-facing teams, San Francisco. Its release of 2020-03-26: Kleiner Perkins led the $7M Series A ($10M raised to date). Momentum check 2026-09-30 (web search): the latest round found is the $25M April 2021 round led by Insight Partners with Kleiner Perkins; no $1B round, and no sale or shutdown found.

Pavilion Data Systems, NVMe-over-fabrics storage arrays (San Jose), on the firm's 2018-25 enterprise and hardtech lists. Its domain is now for sale (2026-09-30) and no sale or shutdown was cited, so status unknown; the round Kleiner Perkins entered is not on record.

PayMate, the Indian mobile and B2B payments company (Mumbai, Wikipedia); the Wikidata NO claim is a homonym, disputed. An iFund position (2008-14 listings). It filed a DRHP in May 2022 but has not listed. The round is not on record.
PeakStream, a software platform for GPU and multicore computing (Redwood City, Matt Murphy); acquired by Google in 2007. The Kleiner Perkins round is not cited, so undetermined.

Pelago, Inc. (the Whrrl location app), Seattle. Wikipedia: its November 2006 Series A was backed by Kleiner Perkins, Trilogy Equity Partners and Bezos Expeditions; Groupon bought it in April 2011. The Pelago rows in the a16z, Atomico, EQT Ventures and YC books are a different company (New York health).
Peng Peng (pengpeng.la), on the firm's 2021-24 logo grid only. The domain no longer resolves and no source read says what the company is or where it is, so the row cannot be identified.

PernixData (flash virtualization), San Jose. Wikipedia: its second round, in May 2013, came from Kleiner Perkins and the original investors, so the firm entered at the B (Growth). Nutanix bought it in 2016.
PiCloud, Python cloud computing (San Francisco, Matt Murphy); Dropbox took it over in November 2013 (aligned with a16z's row). The round is not on record.

Pillar, a student-loan repayment app (founders Michael and Gilad); the JP claim is a Wikidata homonym, disputed. The firm's post of 2019-05-30 announces its investment without naming the round; the firm now lists it among alumni and pillar.app is parked for sale (2026-09-30). Fate and city not found.
Pinger (Textfree, Sideline), founded 2005 by Greg Woock and Joe Sipher, headquartered in San Jose (Wikipedia); an iFund-era listing with Randy Komisar, still operating. The round is not on record.

Plastiq, card-funded bill payment for SMBs, San Francisco. The firm's post of 2018-11-19 says it led the $27M Series C; its listings begin in 2018 and no earlier Kleiner Perkins round is known (Growth). Chapter 11 in May 2023 with the business sold to Priority Technology: acquired with a successor, as Khosla's row.
Platial, collaborative map-making website, Portland OR; it announced its closure on 2010-02-27 (Wikipedia). The round the firm entered is not on record.

Plum District, daily deals for mothers, San Francisco; an sFund position (Aileen Lee). Wikipedia: $8.5M Series A from Kleiner Perkins and General Catalyst after a $2.1M angel Series A, and a $20M Series C in December 2011; the year of the $8.5M is not given there and is read as 2010, the sFund's launch year. Acquired by Coupon Lawn in July 2020 (Wikipedia), fresher than General Catalyst's 'unknown'.

PodShow (Mevio from 2008), podcast network founded 2004 in San Francisco. Wikipedia: Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia and Sherpalo put in about $8.85M in August 2005, its first venture round; the 2006 round is the second and the 2008 one is named Series C, so the entry is the Series A. The company moved to Hollywood as Bitesize (2012), closed the Mevio service in April 2014, and Bitesize was bought by Media General: acquired, last city Los Angeles.

Poetic (runbooks written in plain language, run by AI; founder Markie Wagner). The firm's post of 2026-06-10: its partner backed Poetic at the seed stage, then Kleiner Perkins led the $50M Series A, which graduates the row; the seed is dated only by the firm's since-year, 2026. Momentum check 2026-09-30 (Google News, nq.py): the headlines of 2026-06-10 (Benzinga, Pulse 2.0) put the Series A at a $500M valuation; no $1B round. The publisher links were not yet decoded, so the check is recorded here only.

Power Computing, the Mac-clone maker founded 1993 in Milpitas and later based across I-35 from Dell's Round Rock campus; Apple bought its Mac OS license and core assets in 1997 (Wikipedia), which ended the business: read as acquired, as the firm's exit line. The firm dates its entry 1995; the round is not on record.
